heard: A billion-year-old star is glowing with elements that decay in decades. Our own sun is mostly hydrogen, with heavier elements making up less than 1% of its mass. Located 356 light-years away in the southern constellation Centaurus, Piaarzybilski's star completely flips that familiar recipe. In 1961, astronomer and Tony Piaarzybilski found rare-earth metals like a holmium enriched by over 1,000 times solar levels. Later studies reported even stranger things, short-lived radioactive elements like promethium, which decays in under 18 years. That sparked wild theories of alien civilizations dumping radioactive waste inside. But overlapping light patterns likely explain away the radioactive elements. Researchers are still investigating the seemingly impossible chemical makeup of this.
differences: 'antoni przybylski' heard as 'and tony piaarzybilski' after 'in 1961 astronomer'
